briefdescription.para: Marmot's own scalar-mode forward automatic differentiation: hyper-dual and univariate Taylor numbers.

listitem.para: ScalarMode::Dual< T > is a dual number whose value and derivative are of type T, either double or a Dual itself. Nesting gives hyper-dual numbers of any order (ScalarMode::HyperDual< order >), which carry one independent direction per nesting level and all mixed derivatives. Level 1 is the outermost one. A Dual is a dense array of 2^order doubles: the value node, followed by the derivative node.
ScalarMode::Taylor< order > is a univariate truncated Taylor polynomial, which carries the derivatives 0..order of one variable.

detaileddescription.para: Both are plain (eagerly evaluated) number types without expression templates, so they may be stored in auto and returned from functions with deduced return types. Elementary functions of Taylor numbers evaluate the transcendental function once, at the value, and compose its Taylor series with the argument.
Use this header through the backend-neutral vocabulary of MarmotAutomaticDifferentiationTypes.h (dual, dual2nd, dual3rd, HyperDual, Taylor, seed, derivative, value, taylorDerivatives).

codeline.highlight: DualComparable=(isDual< A >&&(isDual< B >||Constant< B >))||(Constant< A >&&isDual< B >);
TaylorComparable=(isTaylor< A >&&(isTaylor< B >||Constant< B >))||(Constant< A >&&isTaylor< B >);
